This class follows the full Primary Series, as taught by the late Pattabhi Jois of Mysore, India.

A 90 Minute Ashtanga Primary Series!

Powerful and dynamic, Ashtanga is a strong form of Hatha Yoga, often regarded as the modern day form of classical Indian Yoga.

Practised in the correct sequential order, the Ashtanga system is said to lead the practitioner to rediscover their full potential on all levels; physical, psychological and spiritual. And on the journey there expect to work hard, sweat loads and float home feeling super-light and smiley.

Other modern styles of Yoga such as Yoga Flow or Vinyasa (the linking of movements with breath) are generic names which mostly have their roots in Ashtanga. So if you've practised any of these styles, chances are you'll already be familiar with parts of Ashtanga sequence.

This class follows the full Primary Series, as taught by the late Pattabhi Jois of Mysore, India.

Discover the precision and transformative power of Iyengar Yoga.

B.K.S. Iyengar played a pioneering role in bringing yoga to the Western world, developing a method renowned for its precision, intelligent sequencing and emphasis on alignment. Today, becoming an Iyengar Yoga teacher requires years of dedicated study through a traditional mentor-based training, preserving the depth and integrity of this respected lineage.

Start the new year by deepening your practice in this uplifting Iyengar Yoga workshop. Together we’ll explore the foundations of key postures, discovering how greater awareness, alignment and stability can unlock strength, freedom and ease in the body. As the practice progresses, you’ll build confidence and develop the skills to move towards more dynamic and integrated asanas.

Whether you’re curious about Iyengar Yoga or looking to refine your existing practice, this workshop offers a welcoming and inspiring introduction to its unique approach.

Suitable for students with some previous yoga experience, including those who are new to Iyengar Yoga.

title: The Art of Less: A Rest Yoga Immersion with Tania Moutinho
description:
The Art of Less: A Rest Yoga Immersion

with Tania Moutinho

Sun 21 Feb 2026 | Barefoot Birmingham Harborne Studio

At the deepest month of Winter season, you are invited to rebel!

Step away from the relentless, production-focused noise of the Modern World, and a chronically overwhelmed society, to slip into a Sanctuary of D e e p R e s t .

This mini-retreat is a soft landing nest for you to experience Vishranti, a conscious therapeutic necessity to rest in Ayurveda, and what the Italians call ‘dolce far niente’: the exquisite sweetness of doing absolutely nothing.

February’s cold days offer the perfect natural invitation to regulate our nervous system through quietness. Immerse yourself in our lovely, cosy studio, transformed into a candlelit nest,... and feel the frantic pace of your life simply melt away... into a state of absolute Relaxation... free from guilt.

Your Journey Into Doing Less:

- Gentle, fluid movement: to untangle physical tension, and drift away rigidity

- Soft, spacious stretches: to invite your body’s natural energy to flow lovingly

- Melting into supported Yin poses: wrapped in a cocoon of comfort, to hold space for internal Stillness

- Soothing Pranayama (breathwork): to whisper safety to your nervous system, anchoring you deeper into a restorative state

- An immersive Yoga Nidra (yogic sleep): to take you into the Sweetness of doing Nothing, and the peaceful edge of dreams

- A gentle meditation: to gather the quiet wisdom of the season

All for you to leave feeling profoundly restored, refreshingly connected to your true self, and ready to make the most of your year.

To ensure your absolute comfort, we invite you to create your own personal nest: wrapping yourself in your own familiar layers adds an extra touch of comfort to your practice. You can bring along your favourite cosy essentials: your yoga mat, your softest cushion, your fluffiest blanket, one or two blocks, and a strap. Not essential, but you are also very welcome to bring a bolster if you have one.

Some yoga experience is appreciated, but all are warmly welcome.

title: Headstand Yoga Workshop
description:
Headstand Yoga Workshop

with Jon M.

Sat 8 May 2027 | Barefoot Birmingham Harborne Studio

Fed up of hearing your teacher say 'If headstand is in your practice, go on up' ...while you're face down in Child's pose thinking, 'how do I get it into my practice' ?

We've all been there. Even Jon Moult. Thing is, your regular teacher isn't being slack or lazy with their words. Going up into Headstand takes a lot of time and cannot be taught quickly. You could say it's a practice in its own right. That's why we're running a whole workshop on Sirsasana or 'King of Asanas', as Headstand is often called.

Headstand isn't an essential part of a yoga practice, but its benefits are many and varied, for both mind and body.

If it's a posture you'd like to explore, this workshop offers a playful, safe and supportive environment to do just that. The focus is not on achieving the perfect Headstand, but on drills and tips n tricks to help you experience and integrate the mechanics of the posture. Expect to build strength, confidence, balance and have a lot of fun in the process.

Whether Headstand is something you're trying to learn, or something you'd like to revisit, what better way to spend a Saturday afternoon :-)

Please note: Headstand is not suitable during pregnancy or for anyone with uncontrolled high blood pressure, glaucoma, or certain neck, shoulder, spinal or other health conditions; if you have any concerns, please check with your healthcare professional before attending.
